# 1. LOAD THE DATASET FROM WINDOWS DOWNLOADS
# Points directly to the location you provided
dataset_path = r"C:\Users\Nisha\Downloads\archive (4)\Twitter_Data.csv"

print("[INFO] Loading dataset from path...")
# Read dataset, drop empty text rows, and sample it safely for laptop RAM performance
df = pd.read_csv(dataset_path)
df.dropna(subset=[df.columns[0], df.columns[1]], inplace=True)
df = df.sample(n=50000, random_state=42).reset_index(drop=True)

# Rename columns to standard references for clean variable handling
df.columns = ['clean_text', 'category']
# Convert labels to string integers to manage negative indexes cleanly
df['category'] = df['category'].astype(int).astype(str)

In [5]:
# 2. EXPERIMENT WITH MULTIPLE PREPROCESSING VARIATIONS (Requirement 2)
def preprocessing_variation_1(text):
    """Variation 1: Standard lowercase text processing + Web URL removal."""
    text = str(text).lower()
    text = re.sub(r'https?://\S+|www\.\S+', '', text) # Remove URLs
    text = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z\s]', '', text)          # Keep alphabetical letters only
    return text

def preprocessing_variation_2(text):
    """Variation 2: Advanced text cleaning + Active Stopword Removal."""
    text = preprocessing_variation_1(text)
    # Tokenize words and filter out standard linguistic stopwords
    words = text.split()
    filtered_words = [word for word in words if word not in stop_words]
    return " ".join(filtered_words)

print("[INFO] Applying preprocessing variation matrices...")
df['text_var1'] = df['clean_text'].apply(preprocessing_variation_1)
df['text_var2'] = df['clean_text'].apply(preprocessing_variation_2)

[INFO] Applying preprocessing variation matrices...
In [6]:
# 3. BUILD MODEL PIPELINES & VECTORIZATION MATRIX (Requirement 1 & 3)
# Split data into train and test branches for Variation 1
X_train_v1, X_test_v1, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(df['text_var1'], df['category'], test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
# Split data into train and test branches for Variation 2
X_train_v2, X_test_v2, _, _ = train_test_split(df['text_var2'], df['category'], test_size=0.2, random_state=42)

# Vectorize raw texts using TF-IDF strategy
vectorizer_v1 = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=5000)
vectorizer_v2 = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=5000)

X_train_tfidf_v1 = vectorizer_v1.fit_transform(X_train_v1)
X_test_tfidf_v1 = vectorizer_v1.transform(X_test_v1)

X_train_tfidf_v2 = vectorizer_v2.fit_transform(X_train_v2)
X_test_tfidf_v2 = vectorizer_v2.transform(X_test_v2)

# Model Version A: Naive Bayes Classifier
nb_model = MultinomialNB()

# Model Version B: Logistic Regression Classifier
lr_model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)

# Train and predict Version A (Naive Bayes) over Preprocessing Variation 1
nb_model.fit(X_train_tfidf_v1, y_train)
nb_preds = nb_model.predict(X_test_tfidf_v1)

# Train and predict Version B (Logistic Regression) over Preprocessing Variation 2
lr_model.fit(X_train_tfidf_v2, y_train)
lr_preds = lr_model.predict(X_test_tfidf_v2)

# 4. PRINT PERFORMANCE METRICS & ACCURACY TABLES (Requirement 3)
print("\n" + "="*70)
print("          TASK 3: NLP SENTIMENT MODEL METRICS EVALUATION")
print("="*70)

# Calculate explicit macro F1 scores
nb_f1 = f1_score(y_test, nb_preds, average='macro')
lr_f1 = f1_score(y_test, lr_preds, average='macro')

# Calculate explicit accuracy metrics
nb_acc = accuracy_score(y_test, nb_preds)
lr_acc = accuracy_score(y_test, lr_preds)

# Direct markdown comparison visual table print output
print(f"{'Model Configuration Version':<45} | {'Accuracy':<8} | {'Macro F1-Score'}")
print("-"*70)
print(f"{'Naive Bayes (Preprocessing Var 1 - Basic)':<45} | {nb_acc*100:.2f}%  | {nb_f1:.4f}")
print(f"{'Logistic Regression (Preprocessing Var 2 - Stopwords)':<45} | {lr_acc*100:.2f}%  | {lr_f1:.4f}")
print("="*70)

print("\nSUCCESS!! Task 3 matrix pipeline completed successfully.")

# Sentiment distribution Bar charts
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd
# counting the distrubution of prediction of my high-performing model.
sentiment_counts = pd.Series(lr_preds).value_counts()
label_mapping = {'-1': 'Negative', '0': 'Neutral', '1': 'Positive'}
sentiment_counts.index = sentiment_counts.index.map(label_mapping)
# category ordering
ordered_categories = ['Negative', 'Neutral', 'Positive']
counts = [sentiment_counts.get(cat, 0) for cat in ordered_categories]
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

ax = sns.barplot(x=ordered_categories, y=counts, palette=['#ff6b6b', '#ffd166', '#06d6a0'])
# title and axit markers
plt.title('Distribution of Predicted Sentiments (Logistic Regression Model)', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', pad=15)
plt.xlabel('Sentiment Class', fontsize=11)
plt.ylabel('Number of Social Posts', fontsize=11)

# annotate exact numeric counts on top of each bar
for p in ax.patches:
    ax.annotate(f'{int(p.get_height()):,}', 
                (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()), 
                ha='center', va='center', 
                xytext=(0, 8), 
                textcoords='offset points', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# generate the sentiment word count
import os
try:
    from wordcloud import WordCloud
except ImportError:
    print("[INFO] Installing wordcloud library...")
    os.system('pip install wordcloud')
    from wordcloud import WordCloud
# validation tracking slice of test text and corresponding model prediction
test_df = pd.DataFrame({'text': X_test_v2, 'pred_label': lr_preds})
# sperate positive and negative text structure
positive_words = " ".join(test_df[test_df['pred_label'] == '1']['text'])
negative_words = " ".join(test_df[test_df['pred_label'] == '-1']['text'])

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 8))

# generate positive word cloud
wordcloud_pos = WordCloud(width=600, height=400, background_color='white', max_words=100, colormap='summer').generate(positive_words)
ax1.imshow(wordcloud_pos, interpolation='bilinear')
ax1.set_title('Top Keywords in Positive Sentiments', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax1.axis('off')

# generate negative word cloud
wordcloud_neg = WordCloud(width=600, height=400, background_color='white', max_words=100, colormap='autumn').generate(negative_words)
ax2.imshow(wordcloud_neg, interpolation='bilinear')
ax2.set_title('Top Keywords in Negative Sentiments', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax2.axis('off')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# generating the performance confusion matrix heatmap
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix
# calculate structural multicase confusion values
cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, lr_preds, labels=['-1', '0', '1'])
class_names = ['Negative', 'Neutral', 'Positive']

plt.figure(figsize=(7, 5))
# seaborn heatmap matrix
sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='Blues', xticklabels=class_names, yticklabels=class_names, cbar=False,
            annot_kws={"size": 12, "weight": "bold"})

plt.title('Model Performance Confusion Matrix HeatMap (Logistic Regression)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=15)
plt.xlabel('Predicted Sentiment Labels', fontsize=11)
plt.ylabel('True Dataset Labels', fontsize=11)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
